punchline: In 2012 US airlines kept 37 cents from an average $178 ticket, while Google kept 21 cents of every revenue dollar.
thirty_sec: Peter Thiel puts two numbers side by side in Zero to One. In 2012 US airlines made 37 cents per passenger on an average $178 fare. Google kept 21% of its revenue as profit. The difference, he says, is that airlines compete and Google stands alone. The funny part is how each side hides it: Google calls itself a tiny player in advertising, while small restaurants shrink their market until they look unique.
